objective: Memory provenance in the session loop: a run cites the memory that fed it from its own records, every entry mutation is receipted through the existing owners, and no unreceipted mutation path remains.
falsifiable_claim: npm run check:memory-provenance --workspace=@ioi/hypervisor-app PROBES the direct entry verbs and requires 409 memory_entry_direct_mutation_refused naming both the proposal path and the receipt kind; drives add, supersede and archive through the proposal owner and requires each approval to write a hypervisor.memory-mutation receipt carrying operation, applied_ref and source_authority with receipt_type context_mutation; drives the bulk vault import and requires it to receipt each entry it writes with operation import and its source path; and requires the memory projection to be bound to the session in the DAEMON's own records with included_entry_refs present, so the citation is not a label the surface computed.

code_anchors.literal: an unreceipted mutation path does not exist

adversarial_or_fault_proof: The load-bearing clause is a claim about ABSENCE, which is satisfied by not looking, so the gate probes rather than asserts: it exercises each direct verb and requires a refusal, and exercises the bulk path and requires a receipt. Before this cut all three paths — create, patch and vault import — wrote a memory entry with no receipt at all. It also requires every mutation receipt to be ATTRIBUTABLE (operation, applied ref, source authority), not merely present, so a receipt that records nothing about who or why does not satisfy it.
remaining_nonclaims: 'Delete' means ARCHIVE. There is no DELETE verb on a memory entry and reading the acceptance literally would have invented one; the archive proposal is the delete this unit claims.
Skills and affinities keep their direct create/patch verbs. The unit's scope is the memory-entry and memory-mutation owners, and closing the shared helper for every family would have gone beyond it.

The citation proves the projection is BOUND to the session in the daemon's records and carries included_entry_refs. It does not claim the consumer session lane currently mints projections: the M13.4 rebound path does not touch memory, and projections are minted by the GoalRun and agent-launch lanes.

The thread and agent memory lanes (/v1/threads/:id/memory, /v1/agents/:id/memory) return receipt-shaped strings that are minted rather than persisted. They are a separate owner and are untouched here.
